author: reek
body: A listing with no disk attached returns the empty list, so a correct implementation and a broken one are indistinguishable without a disk. This test attaches one: fat16-list.disk is a GPT image whose FAT16 ESP holds CODEX.CDX in the root and BOOTX64.EFI inside EFI/BOOT, so it pins the root listing, the subdirectory walk, the file/directory split and the extension filter against bytes that are really there.

author: reek
body: It also pins the two answers that were wrong. file-exists returned False for every path on every disk, because it guarded on block-sector-count, which reads 0 on a disk that is attached and reads perfectly. And the guard it replaces cannot simply be dropped: with no disk the boot record parses out of zeroes, bytes-per-sector is 0, and the root-directory size divides by it. fat16-init is total now and the volume itself says whether it is usable.
